sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Administration of Employee Share Incentive Plans (ESOP Trusts)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US–France Double Taxation Convention (28 July 1967, as amended by Protocols of 1984, 1994, and 2009)
France–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (21 July 1959, as amended)
France–United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (19 June 2008)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) — provisionally applied since 21 September 2017
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (MLI) — ratified by France on 26 September 2018

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L561-2-2, L561-45 to L561-49 and R561-20-2 et seq. (beneficial-owner definition, declaration, and registry); Décret n° 2017-1094 du 28 juin 2017 (RBE filing mechanics within the RCS); Code de commerce, Articles L123-23 and R123-166 et seq. (RCS maintenance by the greffier); Loi n° 2016-1691 du 1er décembre 2016 (Sapin II) reinforcing UBO verification and asset-freeze powers; Articles L562-1 et seq. CMF (national freezing orders); Article L561-15 CMF (suspicious-transaction reporting to TRACFIN); access to the RBE restricted by Conseil d'État, 15 June 2023, n° 466262, to persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; sanctions for defaulting companies under Article L561-47 CMF.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any foreign corporate member/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization where the origin state is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of valid passport and proof of residential address for each natural-person UBO, gérant, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin (or French notaire upon original document examination)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague origin states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly executed and notarized power of attorney (pouvoir) authorizing the French incorporation agent/signatory to sign the SARL statuts and RCS filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin or Greffe-recognized French legal counsel

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified financial statements or solvency/tax-identification evidence of the corporate member (source-of-funds and commercial-substance verification)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Statutory auditor / certified public accountant of the corporate member
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague origin states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening, conducted pre-engagement and re-run every 12 months or upon any ownership change, of all UBOs (at and above 25%), gérants, and authorized signatories against: (i) French PEP data in line with FATF Recommendation 12 and Article L561-10 CMF; (ii) the EU and UN consolidated sanctions lists; (iii) the OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists where USD payments or US persons are involved; and (iv) French national asset-freeze measures under Articles L562-1 et seq. CMF. Any positive or fuzzy hit is escalated to the designated compliance officer for written reasoned disposition; where the suspicion satisfies Article L561-15 CMF, a déclaration de soupçon must be filed with TRACFIN before proceeding with incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated with the Conseil national des greffiers des tribunaux de commerce; name and trademark ante-validation via the INPI register (data.inpi.fr) and Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr) for RCS and company-extract searches
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SARL name may be in any language but must be rendered in Latin script (or officially transliterated into Latin characters) for RCS registration; the French statutory name and the legal-form suffix 'SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée' must appear on all French-facing legal documents in accordance with the language doctrine of the Code de commerce (Article L123-1 et seq.; Décret n° 2017-923). The name must be distinctive, non-misleading as to the regulated activities actually performed, and must not incorporate protected trademarks or reserved public-order terms.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Avocat / Notaire / Huissier de justice / Expert-comptable
Fiduciaire / Fonds de placement (absent a regulated license)
État / République / Préfecture / Ministère / Collectivité territoriale
France (and French-language equivalents) absent a legitimate corporate identity nexus
Bourse / Marché réglementé / Autorité / Commission (implying regulatory endorsement)
Crédit / Caisse / Prêt (banking-domain terms reserved under banking monopoly regulations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory 'name reservation' registry: distinctiveness is verified by the greffier at the moment of RCS filing. If the article of association is not filed within 30 days of the pre-clearance search, re-run the INPI/RCS ante-validation search before submission (the 30-day recency standard is a due-diligence requirement, not a legal validity period). Upon a refusal of incorporation (refus d'immatriculation) by the greffier—whether for confusing similarity, misleading form, or reserved terms—the applicant may (i) submit written observations to the greffier requesting reconsideration within 15 days of notification; (ii) if the refusal is maintained, file a judicial appeal before the Tribunal de commerce (commercial chamber) in accordance with Articles L123-35 and R123-127 et seq. of the Code de commerce; and (iii) where the conflict concerns a priority trademark, institute or defend opposition proceedings before the INPI. Legal counsel should obtain the greffier's written reasoned rejection and preserve all pre-clearance evidence for the appeal record.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible in the form of legal domiciliation for a maximum of five (5) years per declared address under Article L123-11-1 of the Code de commerce, conditional on a written 'contrat de domiciliation' filed with the greffe and an address physically fit to receive public notifications. Because the ESOP-administration SARL is unlicensed and classified Low_Risk_Standard, domiciliation is acceptable during the start-up phase; however, credit institutions performing AML/KYC on the SARL's French payment and equity-transfer rails will independently verify the substance of the declared seat, and tax authorities may disregard a fictitious siège social under the final paragraph of Article L123-11-1.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 5% annual probability of an unannounced on-site verification during the first 36 months for an unlicensed low-risk SARL; the likelihood rises to roughly 25% upon a tax audit (contrôle sur pièces / vérification de comptabilité), an AML suspicion escalation by the SARL's bank, or inconsistencies between the RBE filing and the domiciliation contract.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name pre-clearance and ante-validation search (INPI trademark + RCS exclusivity screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI) / Greffe du tribunal de commerce (RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory INPI service tariff; nominal greffe search charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified legalization bundle — certified translations (traductions assermentées) of foreign corporate/UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator registered with the Cour d'appel (France)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per translated page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille bundle for three foreign UBO/member identity packages
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in country of origin / competent authority under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular/notarial statutory tariff of the origin jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation AML/KYC and PEP/sanctions screening of 3 UBOs + 2 gérants/signatories (OFAC, UN, EU, French freezing orders)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML compliance officer / avocat conducting customer due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per screened individual + adverse-hit investigation supplement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation contract (siège social) — first-year commitment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed société de domiciliation (approved under Article L123-11-1 and R123-165 Code de commerce)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (€1,500–€2,800 per annum in Île-de-France)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SARL statuts (articles of association) with ESOP-trust governance, share-transfer restrictions, and subordination clauses
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed-fee benchmark (€1,200–€3,000 depending on complexity)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in a Journal d'annonces légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized legal-announcements gazette (JAL) approved by the regional greffe

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration fees (droits d'immatriculation) and integrated UBO/RBE declaration filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce competent for the siège social
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Code de commerce (greffe fee schedule varying by department; RBE filing bundled at no incremental charge)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: K-bis company extract issuance and initial company kit/seal (contingency)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / accredited corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nominal statutory fee and nominal supplier charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization contingency for source-jurisdiction documents from non-Hague-convention states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French consulate in the country of origin / Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the source state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule of the issuing posts (contingency — only triggered if apostille route is unavailable)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL formation, capital, management, and dissolution); French Regulation on the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (Decree No. 2021-1206 et seq.).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) – Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); final registration and K-bis issuance by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the competent competent jurisdiction.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: M0 Form (CERFA) and the notarized or private-signed Statuts (Articles of Association) of the SARL, filed electronically through the Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is prescribed for a French SARL. The capital is freely fixed in the articles. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and at least 20% paid up at incorporation; the balance must be paid within five years. All cash contribution must be deposited into a blocked bank account with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or held by a notary until registration, then released to the gérant.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the members, having irrevocably subscribed the shares of the Company as set forth in the Articles of Association, approve the formation of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée and adopt its Articles in the form initialled ad hoc. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [address], within the jurisdiction of the competent Registrar, and that the gérant named below accept office for an unlimited term. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name], acting as first gérant, be appointed, with general powers to represent the Company, open bank accounts, and carry out all registration and licensing formalities. FURTHER RESOLVED, that any co-founder or attorney-in-fact be authorised to execute and file all statutory declarations and pay all required fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Statuts (Articles of Association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Members (private signed deed) or a Notary (acte authentique) if in-kind contributions or real estate are involved.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts including corporate name, purpose limited to administration of employee share incentive plans (ISIC 6430), registered office, share capital amount and distribution, apports en numéraire or en nature, identity of initial gérant, duration (max 99 years), and dispute resolution clauses. Have all members sign, initial every page, and number the annexes. If any contribution is in kind, obtain a statutory auditor's valuation report and notarize the deed.
required_dossiers: Provisional or final Statuts
Identity documents of each member and the first gérant
Proof of residential address of the gérant
Valuation report of in-kind contributions (if applicable)
Power of attorney for any co-founder signing by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries any statutory clause (e.g., ambiguity in purpose or capital), amend by an extraordinary members' resolution and re-file a neatly consolidated version through the Guichet Unique without incurring new filing fees if submitted within the prescribed correction period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Cash Contributions into a Blocked Account or with a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) or an authorized French bank, or a notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account for the future SARL or use a notarial escrow account. Wire or transfer the subscribed cash amount (minimum 20% of cash contributions; in practice the full amount for simplicity). Obtain an attestation de dépôt des fonds (deposit certificate) issued by the bank or notary, stating the depositor, amount, and purpose.
required_dossiers: Copy of the draft statuts
Identity documents of contributors
Proof of source of funds (for AML compliance)
Banking identification (RIB) of the future company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects a deposit for AML reasons, provide a source-of-funds declaration and documentary evidence, or use an alternative French bank or notarial deposit; the capital deposit must remain blocked until registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a Legal Notice in a French Legal Announcements Journal (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) selected in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the legal announcement containing the corporate name, form (SARL), capital amount, registered office address, corporate purpose, duration, and names of the gérant. Submit to the JAL and pay the publication fee. Obtain the attestation de parution (proof of publication).
required_dossiers: Copy of the final statuts
Determination of the legal form and capital
Proof of identity of the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects or delays publication due to factual errors, correct the announcement text and republish; the corrected publication may be retroactively effective if made within a short cure window, otherwise the filing step must be rescheduled.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Formation File via the Guichet Unique (M0 and Annexes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI – Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an online account on the portal and complete the M0 comprehensive form. Attach the signed statuts, bank certificate of deposit, legal announcement proof, proof of registered-office occupancy (lease, owner consent, or domiciliation contract). Declare the beneficial owner and provide proof of identity. Submit electronically; the system assigns a trackable reference and automatically routes to the competent registry, tax, and social authorities.
required_dossiers: Fully signed Statuts (final version)
Attestation de dépôt des fonds (bank or notary certificate)
Attestation de parution in a JAL
Proof of enjoyment of the registered office (lease/domiciliation contract)
Identity and address documents of directors and shareholders
Declaration of non-conviction for the gérant (or declaration of beneficial ownership)
Completed M0 form with signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Guichet Unique automatically notifies for incompleteness; the applicant generally has 15 days to provide missing documents. A corrected resubmission within that window without a new fee is permitted. If the file is rejected for statutory incompatibility, amend the statuts or provide a memorandum of explanation to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Commercial Court Registry and Issuance of the K-bis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the compétent territorial jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validated transmission from the Guichet Unique, the registry performs the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) registration. The company is allocated a SIREN and a SIRET number and is formally registered under the RCS. The registry issues the Extrait K-bis, which is the official proof of legal existence and corporate capacity.
required_dossiers: All dossiers already transmitted via the Guichet Unique
Proof of deposit of capital
Legal announcement attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the file (e.g., inconsistent purpose or invalid appointment of gérant), respond with a corrective supplementary filing within the specified cure period. Payment of a supplementary registry fee may apply if the request arises post-registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Formalities: Tax, Social, and Equity Plan Notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and URSSAF; possibly the AMF if the ESOP trust will hold listed securities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the K-bis is obtained, verify that the company is registered for corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) and for payroll taxes with URSSAF. If the employee share incentive trust will involve listed French securities or investments in regulated financial products, file a notification with the AMF or DREETS, depending on the plan structure. Appoint a tax representative if needed.
required_dossiers: Extrait K-bis
Bank certificate after release of capital
Identity documents of the tax filer/representative
Plan documents of the ESOP trust
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or social registration is delayed, contact the Guichet Unique or the DGFiP with the file reference; missing K-bis or corporate proof must be reissued or rectified. Any late filing can be cured by filing a grace-period declaration under the procedural rules of the DGFiP.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the entity conducts administrative financial services as an employee share ownership trust under ISIC 6430, not manufacturing or physical operations. For a dedicated office only, the general jurisdiction of DREETS applies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no operational or manufacturing permit is required under French industrial classification for the administration of employee benefit trusts.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique / DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity (ISIC 6430, NAICS 525920) is not an installation classée (ICPE) and does not require any prior environmental authorization or EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no industrial wastewater, atmospheric emissions, VOC, or solid waste generation. Compliance with general office-waste sorting under the Circular Economy Law (AGEC) is sufficient.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable – no industrial civil-defense clearance or fire-safety certification is required for a pure administrative ESOP trust. The standard workplace safety and fire-prevention rules of the French Code du travail (Articles L.4121-1 et seq.) and local fire safety regulations for tertiary office premises apply, including suitable evacuation and smoke-detection measures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) under the Ministry of Economy and Finance; principal online portal: impots.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity without a French permanent establishment must apoint a VAT representative established in France and submit the registration application to the DGFiP via Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) using Cerfa form n° 15903 (corporate tax filing registration) and Cerfa form n° 11263*01 (TVA/VAT registration). The application must provide the foreign entity's certified constitutional documents, proof of economic activity in France or French taxable supplies, and identification of the statutory tax representative. Upon issuance, the DGFiP assigns a SIREN number and an intra-Community TVA identification number (FRXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX), which must be stated on all tax filings and customer invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under French law. SARLs are default corporate taxpayers subject to corporate income tax (IS) under Article 206 of the Code Général des Impôts. A SARL may opt for partnership-style transparency under Article 239 bis AA or Article 239 bis AB only in strictly limited statutory circumstances (e.g., newly created enterprises or SARL holding companies meeting specific conditions), which makes the profits taxable directly in the hands of the individual shareholders. Hybrid mismatch adjustments apply under the ATAD rules as implemented in the CGI (Article 205 A, 209 B and related provisions), limiting deduction of payments that give rise to hybrid mismatches. No available check-the-box election exists for non-resident shareholders to alter SARL classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic TVA franchise thresholds: EUR 85,000 for principal supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for principal supplies of services. Optional simplified reporting applies to small businesses; for intra-Community distance sales and electronic services supplied to non-taxable persons the distance selling threshold is EUR 10,000. Foreign suppliers with taxable supplies in France must register for TVA immediately without entitlement to the franchise below these thresholds when a French taxable nexus exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: From the 2026-2027 e-invoicing reform, domestic B2B invoices must be issued electronically in Factur-X, UBL, or CII formats and transmitted through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) approved by the DGFiP. Real-time fiscal clearance (pre-clearance or digital stamping) is not implemented; instead, transaction data must be reported periodically through the PPF in the required E-Report format. Exports continue to require the issuance of an electronic export invoice and may be cleared through the DELTA/Douane processes, but no separate VAT digital stamp applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exported goods that are physically dispatched outside the European Union, provided the exporter receives proof of departure within 12 months of dispatch (CGI Art. 262-I). Exporters must hold a valid customs export declaration and transport evidence showing exit from the EU. Intra-Community supplies of goods to a VAT-registered customer are also zero-rated where the French supplier states the customer's EU VAT identification number and satisfies Art. 262 ter CGI conditions. Offshore services (B2B) fall outside French VAT jurisdiction when supplied to a business established outside France or when the customer is liable for VAT in the country of establishment; for services supplied to a taxable person established in the EU, the reverse-charge mechanism shifts VAT to the customer. The ESOP trust acting as administrative intermediary must document the specific service or goods flow and retain signed declarations from its foreign clients to support a zero-rated or no-VAT position.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Proof of Physical Export (CMR / Airway Bill / Electronic Transport Document)
Export Evidence Certificate issued by the DGFiP (if specifically requested)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration routinely scrutinises export zero-rating claims and requires full documentary support. If export formalities are absent or fraudulent, TVA may be immediately reclaimed from the taxpayer together with interest at 0.20% per month (retard), a 40% penalty for bad-faith failure, and an 80% penalty for abuse or manoeuvres frauduleuses under Article 1729 CGI. Penalties can be raised to 100% in cases of fraudulent collections. Criminal liability under Articles 1741 and 1743 of the CGI follows for false declarations, with penalties of up to EUR 750,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years. The reassessment window is extended from the ordinary 3-year period to 10 years for tax fraud and when the taxpayer is subject to anti-abuse investigation; VAT credit refunds arising from zero-rated exports may be clawed back with retroactive effect plus interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB); banking supervision and AML/CFT oversight is exercised by the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR); exchange control and external financial reporting is administered by the Direction Générale du Trésor under the French Monetary and Financial Code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a eurozone member state; the euro is fully convertible for current and capital account transactions. Capital movements within the EEA are unrestricted under EU Treaty liberalisation; transactions with non-EEA jurisdictions are generally free subject to statistical reporting, tax transparency declarations and, in exceptional circumstances, EU safeguard or selective restriction measures. Profit remittance and dividend distribution to non-resident shareholders are not subject to FX conversion approval; however, a French SARL acting as an ESOP trust must evidence the source of funds and the underlying share-plan documents for the bank's compliance assessment. The effective hurdles are AML/KYC and OECD/FATCA reporting, not exchange control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any mandatory surrender, forced conversion or timeline for export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency in a designated account or convert to EUR freely. For statistical balance-of-payments purposes, the French resident must report to the Banque de France any cross-border financial transaction with a non-EEA counterparty that exceeds the regulatory de minimis threshold using the monthly External Financial Reporting (EFR/LaREP) channel; the reporting deadline is the 15th business day following the month in which the transaction settles. The appointed French bank typically files this declaration on behalf of the resident for export receipts, thereby removing the necessity for a separate client-side filing.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: For an ESOP trust established as a French SARL, non-French Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) authorised in an EEA state may passport into France under ACPR/EBA rules, but must have a registered agent or branch; offshore EMIs outside the EEA are considered high risk and are not permitted to provide settlement services in EUR or maintain French securities accounts without a full ACPR licence. Feasibility rating: Medium for ACPR or EEA-passported EMIs; Low for non-EEA digital-only providers. Legal constraints include the requirement for a licensed custody or escrow arrangement when holding employee share proceeds, and compliance with Article L.525-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code prohibiting unlicensed money transmission.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not an absolute statutory mandate. ACPR has accepted remote corporate onboarding via compliant video identification (Decree 2018-1125) where the director and ultimate beneficial owner are verified with a valid identity document and a live interview. However, for a trust-like ESOP structure, French banks will typically require at least one face-to-face meeting for the primary signatory, or a high-grade remote interview with notarised and apostilled corporate deeds. In practice, for a new SARL opening an escrow account, a physical visit to the corporate desk in Paris or the regional commercial centre is imposed unless the bank offers a documented 'Distance Corporate Opening' pathway. The mandate generally requires a French-speaking manager or a certified translator during the KYC interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident legal owner and complex trust chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current K-bis extract dated less than three months; certified copy of the trust deed and ownership schedule; group organigram showing all intermediate vehicles; statutory representation documents for each layer; valid passports, proof of address and tax residence for the manager and every beneficial owner above the 25% threshold; notarised board resolution appointing account signatories; legal opinion on the validity of the ESOP trust under French or foreign law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Employee stock ownership trust activity flagged as high net-worth financial vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business description aligned with ISIC 6430 and NAICS 525920; full documentation of the approved employee share incentive plan; option or restricted share unit agreements; latest annual accounts or interim financial pack; independent valuation report for the underlying shares; source-of-wealth statements for initial contributions; written confirmation that the entity performs no deposit-taking and no credit transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to or from non-cooperative jurisdictions or high-risk payees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying commercial documentation, including vesting notices, share purchase contracts and payroll disclosure forms; KYC file on the immediate counterparty including certified corporate records; ultimate beneficial owner register; OECD CRS and FATCA self-certifications; tax legal opinion confirming the absence of illegal offshore structuring; for payees in a high-risk jurisdiction, an additional sanction-screening report and declaration of the expected purpose of the transaction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound contributions to the ESOP trust's French capital account are routed through the SWIFT network using MT103 customer credit transfers with EU Balance of Payments purpose code G160 for direct investment in equity or G170 for direct investment loans, accompanied by the underlying share-plan or financing agreements. For EU/EEA-origin funds, SEPA Credit Transfers settled on Target2 are acceptable; for non-EEA contributors, the French bank may require an advance foreign-exchange declaration to the Banque de France when the transaction exceeds the regulatory threshold. All inbound flows undergo payment screening, source-of-funds verification and sanctions filtering. Where the contribution forms part of a foreign direct investment in a French company, the additional thresholds and screening of the EU Regulation on Foreign Direct Investment may trigger a notification to the Direction Générale du Trésor if the ESOP trust acquires a controlling interest in a sensitive sector.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound operational disbursements and participant distributions are cleared primarily via SEPA payments for EUR-denominated transfers within the EEA, and via SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA beneficiaries; for large banking transfers, MT202 covers interbank settlement. Documentary commercial letters of credit and standby letters of credit may be opened using MT700 messages for cross-border share purchases and trade settlement. The preferred rails are: Target2/SWIFT gpi for traceability, French CVA/SEPA Payroll Payment Scheme for recurring employee distributions, and MT103 in strict SWIFT-compliant format for non-EEA wire transfers. The trust will use its operational account ledger to maintain transaction identifiers and file the required monthly Banque de France statistical reports for outbound flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forward contracts with a tenancy of one to twelve months, executed through an ACPR-authorised credit institution
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for non-convertible or less-liquid emerging market currencies, executed through a licensed counterparty with appropriate ISDA and CSV collaterals
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for synthetic EUR / USD / GBP funding structures
Vanilla FX options and zero-premium collars
Cross-currency basis swaps for long-term ESOP trust foreign-currency exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SARL; no filing authority receives the approval resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each financial year, unless an extension is granted by the competent court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order may compel approval and impose a daily penalty; managers may incur civil or criminal liability for persistent non-compliance. No automatic fixed strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval, or within two months where filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction, daily coercive fine, and a potential fine of up to EUR 1,500, doubled for repeat non-compliance. Prolonged inactivity or unresolved registry irregularities may lead to administrative removal proceedings, but no automatic statutory strike-off period is prescribed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December; electronic filing deadlines may be adjusted annually by the Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest and tax surcharges generally apply, including a 10% surcharge for late filing absent a formal notice and higher penalties in cases of formal notice, concealment, or fraud. Administrative strike-off is not an automatic consequence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information review and amendment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Trade and Companies Register through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation filing is required; changes to beneficial ownership or control information must generally be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered compliance, potential criminal penalties for inaccurate or omitted information, and possible registry or banking restrictions. No automatic annual strike-off rule applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate records and management review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records maintained at the registered office; available to competent authorities upon lawful request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually, covering shareholder resolutions, management changes, share transfers, registered-office details, beneficial ownership, and statutory books
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Management liability, evidentiary disadvantages, and potential regulatory or judicial orders. No separate annual government renewal fee or automatic strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory auditor appointment or continuation, if thresholds or group conditions are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; appointment and relevant corporate information are reflected in the Commercial Court Registry records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before the statutory audit obligation begins and maintained for the required mandate period; reassessment is required for each financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a required statutory auditor may result in court appointment, criminal and civil liability for managers, and inability to validly complete required audited reporting.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally required where the SARL exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the relevant statutory assessment date: EUR 5 million total balance sheet assets, EUR 10 million net annual turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional rules may apply to parent companies, subsidiaries, or entities forming a qualifying group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority regulations, principally the French Chart of Accounts. IFRS is not generally mandatory for an unlisted SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a separate annual beneficial ownership confirmation filing. The company should perform an annual internal verification of shareholders, control rights, managers, and beneficial owners. Any change must be reported to the beneficial ownership register generally within 30 days. Share transfers must be documented in the company's corporate records and reflected in registry filings where legally required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register or record of shareholder ownership and share transfers, as applicable to the SARL
Register of shareholder and management resolutions or minute book
Annual accounts, inventory, and supporting accounting records
Current articles of association and amendments
Corporate records evidencing managers, registered office, beneficial owners, and share capital

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 550-2,200 per year for a standard registered-office or domiciliation arrangement; no general French annual registered-agent renewal fee applies
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-12,000 per year where a statutory auditor is required, depending on turnover, transaction volume, group reporting, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover < €10 million; Research Tax Credit (CIR) and Innovation Tax Credit (CII) available; 3.3% social surcharge on corporate tax exceeding €763,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (annual corporate income tax return) filed electronically via EFI (Echange de Formulaires Informatisés) on impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, deadline is the second business day after 1 May; for other fiscal year-ends, within three months of the year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit (bénéfice net) before tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French-source income only; apply treaty provisions if applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net loss (perte nette) before tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report French-source losses; carryforward rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductions and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all French-source income; deduct expenses directly related to French operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax due (25% standard rate or 15% reduced rate for eligible SMEs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply reduced rate if turnover < €10 million and profit ≤ €42,500; otherwise standard rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of tax due plus 0.5% monthly interest; additional fixed penalty of €150 for failure to file; criminal sanctions for intentional omission.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (for corporate shareholders; 30% for individual shareholders including social levies)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident recipient must provide a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) and submit a request for reduced withholding via the 'procédure de réduction à la source' before payment, or claim a refund after payment using Form 5000/5001; treaty rates typically 0-15% depending on jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33% (treaty rates often 0-10%); Interest: statutory 30% (treaty rates often 0-15%).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400 million (annual turnover or total assets) for full Local File/Master File; simplified documentation required for smaller entities.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies substance-over-form and General Anti-Abuse Rules (GAAR); no specific ESR regime, but entities must demonstrate real economic activity to avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of French-source income or overstatement of deductions in corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 40% penalty on understated tax (80% for abuse of right); interest at 0.2% per month; criminal fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for unpaid corporate taxes if found to have participated in fraudulent acts; travel bans and asset freezes possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SARL with no real business activity, no employees, no physical presence, and no substantive decision-making in France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, denial of treaty benefits, 40% penalty for abuse of law; potential nullification of tax advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for tax debts if company is deemed fictitious; criminal charges for fraud if intent proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML controls for ESOP trust operations, or involvement in money laundering through dividend distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million for entities; criminal penalties for directors up to 5 years imprisonment; confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for AML breaches; travel bans and prohibition from managing companies may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain adequate transfer pricing documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing in cross-border transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, 40% penalty on additional tax, plus interest; potential double taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing; criminal sanctions for fraud in extreme cases.
